title: Efficient computation of real-time correlators using Pauli Propagation
authors: Alexander F. Kemper, Raghav G. Jha, Arnab Bachhar, Goksu C. Toga, Mariano Guerrero Perez, Nicholas J. Mayhall
abstract: Pauli propagation has shown promise for classically simulating quantum dynamics by evolving observables directly in the Heisenberg picture. In this work, we investigate its use for computing real-time two-point time-ordered correlators in one- and two-dimensional quantum systems. One major limitation of Pauli propagation is the rapid growth in the number of Pauli strings beyond short times. We overcome this limitation by combining accurate short-time Pauli-propagation data with time extension methods based on a positivity condition and the observation that the dynamics are often dominated by a small number of characteristic frequencies. This combined approach extends correlation functions far beyond the directly accessible time window while avoiding the exponential proliferation of Pauli operators. We demonstrate that the resulting correlators retain the relevant dynamical and spectral information. Our results broaden the regime in which classical methods can reliably probe the real-time dynamics of interacting quantum many-body systems.
summary: The paper introduces a novel, efficient method to calculate real-time correlation functions in interacting quantum spin systems by combining Pauli Propagation with low-rank time extension. This overcomes the severe limitation of operator basis explosion inherent to direct simulation methods. The technique allows for reliable probing of complex dynamics and spectral features in 1D and 2D quantum magnets.
main_problem: The primary goal is the efficient computation of real-time two-point time-ordered correlators, which are essential for linking microscopic quantum theory to measurable macroscopic observables.
main_result: By combining short-time Pauli propagation with low-rank extension methods based on positivity conditions, the authors extend correlation function calculations far beyond the direct computational time window while maintaining spectral accuracy.
method: The core method involves using Pauli Propagation (PP) to evolve operators in the Heisenberg picture, which is then augmented by time extension techniques that exploit the low-rank nature of the dynamics to overcome the exponential growth of Pauli strings. Ground states are approximated using Clifford-Augmented Matrix Product States (CAMPS).
model_or_system: The study focuses on one- and two-dimensional quantum spin systems, specifically utilizing the Heisenberg model Hamiltonian ($H = J \sum \mathbf{X}_i \cdot \mathbf{X}_{i+1}$). Analyses cover both ferromagnetic and anti-ferromagnetic regimes.
key_observables: Time-dependent correlation functions $C(t)$, dynamical structure factor $S(\mathbf{k}, \omega)$, and the static staggered moment $m_s$.
important_parameters: Pauli string truncation parameters ($\epsilon$, $w$), MPS bond dimensions ($D$), and system size ($N$).
main_assumptions: The method assumes that the correlation functions exhibit a low-rank structure, allowing extrapolation from short-time data; it also relies on truncating the Pauli operator basis.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the computational strategy combining PP with CAMPS and low-rank fitting. They show finite-size scaling of excitation spectra ($\omega(\mathbf{k})$) for 2D AFM systems, demonstrating convergence to theoretical limits.
paper_structure: The paper develops a combined numerical framework: first establishing ground state approximations via CAMPS, then using Pauli Propagation for short-time dynamics, and finally applying low-rank fitting/extension techniques to extrapolate results to longer times and higher resolutions.
why_interesting: This work presents an advanced computational toolkit that tackles the fundamental bottleneck of real-time quantum simulation—the exponential growth of operators—by merging established methods (PP) with modern data analysis techniques (low-rank extrapolation).

Overview of the computational strategy developed in this paper. 1) Real-time operator dynamics, truncated on coefficient and weight to control the growth of Pauli strings. 2) Clifford-augmented MPS supplies an accurate, low-bond- dimension approximation of the ground state to measure against. 3) A low-rank positive semi-definite (PSD) fit super-resolves short-time data out to late times, avoiding Pauli explosion. 4) By combining these techniques, we can obtain the dynamical spin structure factor S(k, ω)
